objective: Compose object shapes using interface extends and type intersection (&)
Predict type conflicts resulting in never when intersecting types with incompatible property definitions

stem: Why might a development team prefer `interface Child extends Parent` over `type Child = Parent & { ... }` when composing object shapes in a large project?
options: Extending interfaces using the extends keyword is often more performant for the compiler than composing type aliases with intersections.
Type intersections with `&` cannot combine two object types that have different property names.
Interfaces can only extend classes, while type intersections can only combine primitive types.
Interfaces automatically prevent any two properties from having the same name, while intersections always compile without checking.
